issues.source_quote: Коты в Сапогах
issues.translation_quote: Pusses in Boots
issues.justification: The plural of 'Puss in Boots' is awkward and archaic; the budget joke (cats cut because there is no money for boots) is muddied, and the following 'cats' line is inconsistent.

issues.source_quote: Подождите, Фёдор Петрович, часы бьют, сколько им положено, и из терема выходит кто?
issues.translation_quote: That'll take three cubic meters of timber.
issues.justification: Source 'Три куба на то тёсу' is fine, but 'Wait, Fyodor Petrovich' follows; the joke about the budget/timber is acceptable. However 'Вот!' reply and 'Dispatcher' structure are preserved. (Minor concern only: the clock striking is rendered correctly.)

issues.source_quote: Ансамбль пенсии и пляски! Виноват, простите, ансамль Песни и пляски!
issues.translation_quote: The Pension and Dance Ensemble! Sorry! The Song and Dance Ensemble!
issues.justification: The pun pension/song (пенсии/песни) is partly preserved, but 'Pension and Dance' is weak because 'Song and Dance' is not the established English phrase for the Soviet ensemble name; acceptable but flat.

issues.source_quote: Вся соль! - А при чём тут соль?
issues.translation_quote: The punchline! - What's a punch got to do with it?
issues.justification: The Russian wordplay (salt as the essence of a joke, taken literally) is replaced with a punch/punchline pun that mistranslates the director's confusion and does not match the literal-minded misunderstanding; 'punch' is not a plausible misreading of 'punchline'.

issues.source_quote: Горько, горько! - Что? Горько товарищи, чувствовать, что мы стали на год старше
issues.translation_quote: - Kiss! Kiss! - What? - It's bitter, comrades, to feel we're a year older.
issues.justification: The wedding-toast 'Gorko!' pun is rendered as 'Kiss!' and then 'bitter', so the director's misunderstanding is lost for English viewers; the wordplay doesn't work.

issues.source_quote: Три храбреца, три храбреца в одном тазу
issues.translation_quote: Three brave men, three brave men, in a single tub
issues.justification: Minor register loss; the nonsense nursery-rhyme tone is kept, but 'таз' (basin) is rendered as 'tub' which is acceptable. Low impact.

issues.source_quote: Выходит докладчик!
issues.translation_quote: A speaker comes out!
issues.justification: 'Докладчик' is someone delivering an official report; 'speaker' loses the bureaucratic flavor that makes the punchline funny after Father Frost and the Snow Maiden. 'Report-giver' or 'a lecturer delivering a report' would keep it.

issues.source_quote: Не такое оно у меня уж и серое, как вы думаете
issues.translation_quote: Mine isn't nearly as gray as you think
issues.justification: The line is a mild rebuke, but the translation turns it into a self-flattering retort that does not match Usikov's gaffe about the director's own 'gray matter'; acceptable but slightly off in tone.

issues.source_quote: А и Б играли на трубе!
issues.translation_quote: A and B playing a trumpet!
issues.justification: The reference to the well-known Russian children's riddle ('А и Б сидели на трубе') is lost; the English reads as nonsense with no recognizable allusion, so the mockery of the orchestra's unserious music is not conveyed.

issues.source_quote: Сыграйте мне что-нибудь... Нужно, чтоб музыка тебя так сказать.. Брала!
issues.translation_quote: Music must, so to speak, grip you!
issues.justification: Source plays on 'брала' / 'вела' / 'уводила' (take/lead/lead away); the English 'lead you astray' captures part of it, but the sequence is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Три куба на то тёсу.
issues.translation_quote: That'll take three cubic meters of timber.
issues.justification: Fyodor Petrovich's terse accountant-style clipped remark is turned into a smooth explanatory sentence.

issues.source_quote: Здрасте, тётя Дуся! - Леночка, на репетиции была, мне очень понравилось!
issues.translation_quote: Lenochka, I saw the rehearsal. I loved it!
issues.justification: Speaker attribution is muddled: in the source Aunt Dusya says she was at the rehearsal; fine, but the second 'Thank you' line sequence is slightly confused.

issues.source_quote: Объективные причины!
issues.translation_quote: Circumstances beyond our control!
issues.justification: The bureaucratic jargon is kept, but loses the ironic flavor of Lena's stock phrase; 'Objective reasons!' would preserve the Soviet-speak.

issues.source_quote: Результат эмоций выжимаем!
issues.translation_quote: We're wringing out the emotion!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but loses the sense of 'squeezing out the result of emotions' as a technical-sounding justification.

issues.source_quote: По-поводу всех этих номеров
issues.translation_quote: as for all these acts...
issues.justification: Fine; no issue.

issues.source_quote: С наступающим, Серафим Иванович!
issues.translation_quote: Happy New Year in advance, Serafim Ivanovich!
issues.justification: Slightly stiff; 'Happy New Year' alone would be natural.

issues.source_quote: Пять звёздочек!
issues.translation_quote: Best of all, of course, is five-star!
issues.justification: The brandy-rating joke is kept but 'is five-star' is ungrammatical and awkward; 'five stars' would be clearer.

issues.source_quote: Тося Бурыкину
issues.translation_quote: Tosya Burykina... Tosya Burakina
issues.justification: The source itself varies the name (the announcer's error); the translation preserves it, but there is no indication of the slip, which makes it look like an inconsistency.

issues.source_quote: Они подают большие надежды!
issues.translation_quote: But they're serving up great promise!
issues.justification: The pun on 'подавать надежды' (show promise) versus serving food is mostly kept, but 'serving up great promise' is stilted compared to a natural English wordplay.

issues.source_quote: Ловкость рук и никакого доклада!
issues.translation_quote: Sleight of hand, and no speech!
issues.justification: Fine; no issue.

issues.source_quote: Нежный, как первое в жизни свиданье
issues.translation_quote: Tender as a first date.
issues.justification: 'Date' has an anachronistic, informal feel for a Soviet-era romantic poem; 'first rendezvous' would suit better.

issues.source_quote: Берите маски, берите маски! Лучшие маски карнавала!
issues.translation_quote: Get your masks! Get your masks! The finest masks at the carnival!
issues.justification: Adequate.
